global_decisions.decision: Two deliverables in two apps. D1, the provider Web UI, is the route group /<locale>/provider of the business web app at web.<DOMAIN> (frontend/, client cp-web-portal, portal BFF). D2, the Workshop PWA, is the route group /<locale>/provider of the consumer PWA at pwa.<DOMAIN> (pwa/, client cp-web-consumer, consumer BFF). The Workshop PWA has its own web app manifest (id and scope /<locale>/provider/, start_url /<locale>/provider/today) so it can be added to the home screen as its own app.
global_decisions.why: Owner decision PRV-OQ-01. The consumer PWA already has the BFF, hosted sign-in, upload kit, map, service worker and push, and Reza gets one sign-in for his family car and his shop (Docs/11 Ch.3).
consequences: The consumer BFF forwards a fixed list of provider operations (PRV-BR-08). Docs/40 SEC-WEB-5 and the header comment of pwa/src/server/bff/allowlist.ts change.
Business pushes arrive in the consumer PWA's service worker. Docs/90 line 124 and pwa DI-16 change (PRV-DI-06, PRV-BR-09).
'Open in Web UI' crosses origins: new tab, separate sign-in.
The camera is allowed on the consumer origin (SEC-WEB-4), so no workaround is needed.
global_decisions.checked: pwa/src/server/bff/allowlist.ts refuses every /v1/orgs/{org_id} route except fleet driver routes today. backend/libs/auth has no rule that binds organization operations to a client; tokens carry no roles (SEC-AU-3). The backend confirms this in PRV-BR-08.

global_decisions.decision: The Workshop PWA does: (1) compact onboarding, (2) answer appointment requests, (3) update and close jobs, (4) reply to customers (review replies, approval answers, comments on the shop's content), (5) post before/after photos. Plus sign-in, business switch, Today, notifications and push, language, theme. Every other task is a link 'Open in Web UI' and is not re-implemented.
global_decisions.why: Owner scope of 2026-11-15 plus PRV-OQ-02 and PRV-OQ-03.

global_decisions.decision: The server decides access. Both deliverables show actions from Appointment.allowed_transitions, the caller's role (P* or P+ as each operation's sec line says) and plan entitlements. No rule is copied to the client. A 403 for a staff member shows 'Ask the owner'.
global_decisions.why: Same rule as the fleet option in frontend/README.md.

global_decisions.decision: Phone budgets for the Workshop PWA: the /provider routes add at most 120 KB gzip of route JavaScript on top of the PWA's shared chunks, LCP ≤ 2.5 s on a mid-range phone over throttled 4G, 48 px targets, one primary action per screen, Sunlight theme offered on first run. The map loads only on the location step of the compact onboarding. Photos are resized in the browser to ≤ 2048 px on the long side (about ≤ 600 KB) before media.upload_init.
global_decisions.why: Docs/carpal-design-system: workshop yards, sun, greasy hands, mobile data. Measured in FT1b.

global_decisions.decision: Provider API answers are never cached by the service worker or kept in Web Storage (they carry customer data); the worker's shell cache is wiped at sign-out, as pwa P12 does. Photos are taken through the upload kit's file input with capture.

AI output is always a labelled draft. A person edits and publishes; the client never sends or publishes AI text without a tap. With AI off (flag, plan or consent) the same screens work with empty editors.

Roles are those of Docs/40 §0.5: provider_owner, provider_manager (P+), provider_staff (P*). The team page offers these three. A technician's 'assigned jobs only' is a 'My jobs' filter built from appointment participants.

Components used by both apps live in a new package shared/business-ui (linked like @carpal/i18n): request card, pre-visit report, answer sheets, job status and close form, review card, reply editor with AI draft, approval card, comment thread, showcase composer steps, status chips. They take data and callbacks as props and import no BFF client, router or app shell. Each app wraps them in its own pages. The package is created in PW1 and grows in PW3-PW7; the Web UI stages reuse it.
global_decisions.why: The two deliverables are two apps (PRV-GD-01); this is the default of PU-OQ-01.

global_decisions.decision: Backend work is not done in this plan. Requests are listed in backend_requests with a fallback and handed to backend/BR-update-plan.json (intake_candidates_provider_plan). A frontend stage names the requests it needs and either waits or builds the fallback.

Stage checks only until the end: typecheck, lint, unit and component tests, and a manual smoke of the stage's path against the dev backend. Playwright journeys, axe, performance and security tests of both deliverables run together in FT1a and FT1b.
global_decisions.why: Owner: the plan (PWA and Web UI) is tested together at the final stage.

global_decisions.decision: The layout follows the mockup. A disabled entry has aria-disabled, is skipped by the keyboard, opens no page and calls no operation. Typing the parts used when closing a job is not part of this: it stays enabled.

conventions.stage_size: One stage = one session. Load is rated small, medium or full. A full stage has a split_point: if the session runs long, stop there, report, and continue as '<id>b' in the next session.
conventions.context_rule: Read only the stage's context_to_read. Use the generated operation map of shared/api-contracts instead of re-reading Docs/40 blocks. Copy the pattern of the first finished screen of a kind.
conventions.stage_checks: pnpm typecheck, pnpm lint, pnpm test in every package the stage touched (pwa/, frontend business app, shared/business-ui); manual smoke in FA and EN at 360 px for PW stages and at 1280 px for PP stages. Use Node 24.
conventions.report: Add to progress_log: date, stage, what was built, deviations, backend requests met or replaced by a fallback, notes for the next stage.
